theorem.statement: In linear SO(3)-invariant Gaussian perturbation theory on the canonical coexact carrier, the shell law G^(1)(ell) is determined by the quadratic boundary operator Q = Gamma_eff''[Abar] restricted to the coexact sector. Once Q and the state-to-covariance functional are fixed, G^(1) is fixed.

hawking_kms.Q: Q = Delta_1^coex, state = Hawking KMS on sqrt(Q)

derived: Linearity and Gaussianity alone do not fix G^(1)(ell); they only reduce the problem to the quadratic coexact-sector operator Q = Gamma_eff''[Abar] and the chosen state-to-covariance functional.
The physically determining object is the boundary effective Hessian on the coexact carrier.
verified: Free-field covariance Q=Delta gives pivot n_s = -0.002067888629, far too red.
Ordinary Hawking/KMS on sqrt(Delta) gives pivot n_s = -8958.753929307341, catastrophically wrong.
The determinant-selected Gaussian operator Q=(sqrt(Delta))^(K_gauge/x) gives pivot n_s = 0.963832748117, close to the exact shell target 0.963908639282.
conditional: The physical coexact-sector Hessian is the determinant-selected Gaussian operator rather than the standard free-field Laplacian or ordinary Hawking/KMS generator.
